page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.1-16 is a memory-weighted virtual machine configuration based on the 64-bit Arm architecture. The compute layer is powered by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family, provisioned with 2 virtual CPUs mapped directly to 2 dedicated physical cores. Because the instance uses a single thread per core execution model, it avoids the hyper-threading resource contention typical of simultaneous multithreading systems, ensuring consistent instruction execution.

Memory provisioning is configured at 16.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage and zero GPU accelerators, relying on attached cloud network block volumes for the root filesystem and stateful persistence. Network connectivity is supported by one complimentary public IPv4 address for external ingress and routing.

The single-threaded dedicated core topology on the Ampere platform offers stable throughput and low operational overhead for memory-demanding deployments, eliminating the cost overhead of provisioning unneeded compute capacity simply to acquire memory capacity. A notable tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage, meaning I/O latency depends on network block storage performance. This instance configuration aligns with workloads such as in-memory caches, lightweight relational databases, Redis instances, backend API servers, and Arm-targeted development environments.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.1-16 is a memory-oriented flexible compute instance designed for workloads requiring a high memory-to-compute ratio. Operating on the 64-bit arm64 architecture, the instance provides 2 dedicated physical CPU cores from the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family, running one thread per core without multithreading contention. System memory totals 16.0 GB, establishing an allocation density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The server configuration includes zero hardware accelerators and no bundled local NVMe storage, relying on external network block storage volumes for persistent data retention. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. By delivering dedicated single-threaded Arm execution with elevated RAM density, the instance offers predictable cost efficiency for deployments that prioritize memory footprint over wide multi-core parallelism. The hardware profile serves application caching tiers, small-scale relational or key-value databases, lightweight microservices, and general Arm development environments.
